transcript.answer: I do not know. I cannot read the re-cinq/Otto repository and have no verified knowledge of how Otto authenticates its WebSocket connections, so I cannot confirm what it does or whether it is safe from logging. As general background only (not specific to Otto): the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header is an ordinary request header, so it can be recorded by proxies, load balancers, and servers that log request headers. It is not sanitized like an Authorization header is by many tools. Putting a token there is therefore not inherently safe from logging, though it is generally less exposed than putting the token in the URL query string, which is commonly logged by default.

judgements.reason: The answer explicitly says it does not know how Otto handles this. Its general remark that subprotocol tokens can be logged is not tied to Otto, and it misses the 101-response echo and the hal.v1 marker fix.
